highlights:
[Malta International Contemporary Art Space is at the Forefront of the Country’s Burgeoning Art Scene > The Editors of ARTnews]

This expansive setting allows for quality exhibitions on an ambitious scale, with a program led by Artistic Director Edith Devaney, a former Senior Curator at London’s Royal Academy of Arts for more than 20 years. The inaugural solo show of Joana Vasconcelos filled MICAS with the Portuguese artist’s signature monumental sculptures, while a subsequent exhibition surveyed Milton Avery and his legacy through the work of contemporary artists such as Nicolas Party, Jonas Wood, and Andrew Cranston.

…

In a similar spirit, the upcoming exhibition “A New Life Force,” opening in October 2026, will feature Nathanaëlle Herbelin, Kemi Onabulé, and Megan Rooney, each presenting new paintings inspired by Malta’s culture, geography, and history, while responding to the museum’s distinct architecture and light.

…

Last month, MICAS hosted a two-day symposium on museum architecture, bringing together architects, historians, curators, museologists, and sociologists to examine how contemporary art institutions can inhabit historic sites while creating new forms of cultural and civic engagement.

results.description: The art galleries at MUŻA – The National Community Art Museum – are undergoing a transformation as significant changes are introduced to its permanent exhibitions. In recent weeks, efforts have been concentrated on the first-floor gallery, with the primary goal of offering visitors a broader and more immersive experience of art in Malta.

highlights:
[National Museum of Art - Auberge D’Italie > Significant Changes to MUŻA’s Permanent Exhibitions]

The art galleries at MUŻA – The National Community Art Museum – are undergoing a transformation as significant changes are introduced to its permanent exhibitions. In recent weeks, efforts have been concentrated on the first-floor gallery, with the primary goal of offering visitors a broader and more immersive experience of art in Malta.

Heritage Malta remains committed to ensuring that the museum’s permanent exhibition continues to evolve, preserving and showcasing the contributions of Maltese artists. These changes will also strengthen MUŻA’s role as an educational hub, telling the story of Malta’s artistic heritage and the influences that have shaped it over time. The restructuring follows a chronological approach, tracing art from prehistoric times to the 21st century.
